pages.text: Habilis finds fire. Erectus keeps it - in a $(l)fire pit$(). At the work station, three sticks along the bottom row and one log in the middle, nothing in the slot. Set it down where the band sleeps. A drill worked on bare ground only makes a flash of flame.

A pit burns what you put in it: sticks, branches (any kind), thatch or nest grass - right-click them in, sneak to put in up to eight. Right-click it empty-handed to see what is in it; sneak empty-handed to take the last thing back out.$(br2)To catch it needs $(l)three things in it$() at least, and something to take the spark: $(l)thatch$(), or warm embers.

Then hold a $(l)fire drill$() to it for three seconds (let go early and it is lost). It may not catch - more thatch helps, rain hurts. A burning torch catches it far more easily than a drill.$(br2)Lit, everything in it is fire. Feed it and it keeps: a stick is a minute, thatch half that, a branch two and a half - up to half an hour banked. Rain eats it four times as fast.

Left alone it burns down to $(l)embers$(), and they stay warm a whole day: fill it again and it catches on them easily. After that it is cold ash, which helps only a little.$(br2)Meat laid on a burning pit comes off cooked - or hang it over one (see The Cooking Rack). At night nothing that hunts will come into its light - and a fire kept on your own ground builds your band’s presence there.

A $(l)torch$(): a stick with thatch over the top of it, three twine in the slot. Light it at any fire. Held, it lights the ground round you; it burns down in about ten minutes, faster in rain, and water puts it out.$(br2)Use it on the ground or a wall and it stays there, lighting the camp twice as long. Use it at anything else and it is thrown: whatever it hits catches, and runs.

$(l)Thatch$() put in an unlit pit lies in the bottom of it, under the sticks, and a thread of smoke comes off it - thicker on the warm ashes of the last fire. Thrown on a burning fire, thatch goes up in a column of white smoke that can be seen a long way off.

Ergaster never worked a drill: its fire was always carried from one burning somewhere else - a torch lit at a wildfire or at lava, walked back and put to the pit. That is how an ergaster keeps a fire.

$(l)Kept fire.$() From erectus on, the band keeps the camp's fire: whoever sees a fire pit burning low feeds it, with what they carry, what is in the piles, or dead wood. One who knows fire lights a laid pit at dusk. $(l)Fire-hardening$(): right-click a fire with a sharpened spear four times, or hold it there.
